WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (Bluffside Brewing Co., Meadowlark Business Plus, MN_CSG / Xcel Energy)

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. The caller asks one thing: accept, today, the 50 kW decrease she requested online, with its fee. The scored fee cannot be produced from her request: (a) the fee rule waits on a state the records do not show (contract year 4 ended on 2026-10-12 and has no true-up), so the agent must discover from the published prerequisite sentence that the true-up is owed, work out that only the true-up write brings that state about, and perform it with its own five-factor guarantee computation; (b) the fee itself is a six-factor computation over the request, the filing lines, the new true-up, the term dates and the customer's garden share in another line. Difficulty comes from reading policy, querying ten record types and calculating, never from choosing among similar tools (two hidden tools, different objects).

2. SCOPE. Occupied before: nothing (task 0). Claimed: biz_ext_guarantee_trueup (agent, complete_guarantee_trueup_bd5f1ac2) and biz_ext_decrease_amendment_fee (user, accept_share_decrease_75e61509). Left for task 1: every other biz event (allocation increases, deposits, late fees, estimates, billing corrections) and any new policy on them; task 1 draws 1 prerequisite and factor counts [6,6] and must use different policies and tools.

3. PROBLEM TREE (draw: prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[6,5]; the fee took 6, the true-up 5).
- Root: biz_ext_decrease_amendment_fee (on_request; the customer's own acceptance, owner=user per owner_ruling (a) "signing / accepting a contract amendment").
- Prerequisite: biz_ext_guarantee_trueup (state_due; agent).
- Edge fee -> true-up: kind value_input, gate latest_usage_kwh (the latest true-up's usage_kwh_12m; guaranteed_kwh is read the same way), form state. Prerequisite sentence (affirmative direction, the way a fee desk states that a charge rests on completed records): "The excess-decrease fee of a decrease amendment is fixed only after the records carry a completed true-up for every contract year of the subscription that has ended." Four-point test: ordering connective "only after"; the waited-on side is a record-visible state (a completed true-up row per ended contract year); no tool, policy id or code token; scope "every contract year that has ended" equals the condition. Only one write of this difficulty creates biz_trueup_completed rows (the true-up tool), so the state names exactly one resolving action. Derivation: sentence + find_biz_reviews (years 1-3 only) + activation_date 2022-10-12 (year 4 ended 2026-10-12) + the true-up policy's rule (its write records the year's true-up) -> complete the contract-year-4 true-up first.
- Why false at the opening: initial_state.biz_reviews.<year-3 row>.contract_year = 3 is the latest; activation_date 2022-10-12 + 48 months = 2026-10-12 <= 2026-10-27.
- Resolvable synchronously: the true-up needs only records already on file (credits, prior true-up, utility usage, project yield); the agent books it at the frozen time.
- Deletion sensitivity (run): skipping the true-up leaves year 3 as the latest true-up -> allowance 25%, nothing released, chargeable 30 kW -> fee 1215.00 instead of 301.89; the year-4 review row and its 167.93 guarantee credit are also missing from the terminal state.
- Topological order: true-up (step 12) then acceptance (step 14); single chain, no parallel edges.
- user_scenario never mentions a true-up, review, guarantee or production; her only related line is a passive go-ahead ("If the agent tells you something on the account has to be finalized or recorded before your change can be handled, you say that's fine and to go ahead."). Neither tool checks the other's state (see tools_do_not_block).

4. BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
- biz_evt_annual_trueup.after_anniversary (time): anchor biz_subscriptions.activation_date 2022-10-12, duration params.review_interval_months 12, calendar months, not_before, inclusive. Year 4 ends 2026-10-12; 2026-10-11 would be too early, 2026-10-12 allowed; frozen 2026-10-27 passes.
- biz_evt_annual_trueup.one_review_per_year (dedup): its evidence contract binds biz_reviews.contract_year to a pre-action system value, which cannot exist for a contract year not yet reviewed (BLUEPRINT-KNOWN). Routed around with a declared self-scoped overwrite that restates the same once-per-year rule for guarantee-schedule years; biz_reviews holds no year-4 row, so the write is the first for that year.
- biz_allocation_change governs the fee event with no structured gate (policy_scope); the decrease itself meets the in-force base gates when Meadowlark files it: request received 2026-10-20 is more than 12 whole months after activation (first_change_wait), status active (reduction_status), first subscriber change of contract year 5 (Plus allows 1), leaves 30.00 kW >= min 25.00 kW. Filing calendar MN_CSG monthly, cutoff 10: received after the 10th -> filed 2026-11, effective 2026-12-01.
- biz_benefit_basis: the guarantee credit is a separate ledger line and changes no charge.

5. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target holding: the one biz subscription (80.00 kW). Fee object: the single open allocation-decrease request (outcome received, 50.00 kW, received 2026-10-20). True-up object: contract year 4 of that subscription; measured lines = the 11 biz_credit_posted rows posted after 2025-10-27 up to 2026-10-27 (statement months 2025-10..2026-07 and 2026-09); excluded: the 2025-09 posting of 2025-10-14 (year 3) and earlier rows; no reversals exist. The 2026-08 statement was never reported; an estimated charge (682.49, billed 2026-10-16) stands for it and is not a credit line. Cross-line object: the Garden Business Fixed 15 share (20.00 kW, active) on the same utility account (read only).

6. FACTOR CARD — biz_ext_guarantee_trueup (result 167.93; all-baseline 332.80).
- degradation_schedule (parameter, R5 schedule, R6 values): contract year 4 -> 0.5% step -> 92439 (baseline 92904) -> result 174.35 under baseline.
- excused_statement_months (method, R3): credited months 11 -> prorate 11/12 -> 84736 (baseline 92439) -> 284.08 under baseline. Near-miss: the 2025-09 posting of 2025-10-14 is outside the window; counting it would give 12 months.
- surplus_carryover (method, R5 cumulative guarantee, R6 cap): year-3 excess 15358 above the 4645 limit -> carry 4645 (baseline 0) -> 237.97.
- banked_credit_valuation (parameter, R6): banked share 7.15% -> mean rate 0.1117 (baseline 0.1158) -> 174.09.
- share_size_guarantee_schedule (parameter, R1 share-size band, R6 points): 80.00 kW -> 13.5% (baseline 12.0%) -> 149.27.
FACTOR CARD — biz_ext_decrease_amendment_fee (result 301.89; all-baseline 1800.00).
- usage_decline_allowance (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty garden, R6 values): latest usage 101830 vs peak 149210 = 68.2% <= 75% AND active garden share on the same account -> 50% (baseline 25%) -> 1111.89. Near-miss: before the true-up the latest usage is year 3 (147860, 99%).
- usage_matched_release (method, R4-grounded sizing logic, R6 band): oversized 5.092 kW (6.4%) -> half released 2.546 kW (baseline 0) -> 405.00.
- term_position_rate (parameter, R5 ETF-equivalent cap): final contract year -> min(60, 40) = 40.00 (baseline 60.00) -> 452.84.
- change_depth_multiplier (parameter, R6): 62.5% of the share -> x1.5 (baseline 1) -> 201.26.
- contract_year_timing_multiplier (parameter, R2 timing on the anniversary, R6 values): 0 months into contract year 5 -> x0.75 (baseline 1) -> 402.52.
- share_size_multiplier (parameter, R1 share-size band): 80.00 kW -> x0.9 (baseline 1) -> 335.43.
No factor reads another factor's binding: shared selections (latest usage, share on file, requested kW, average rate) are plain bindings; every factor acts on a quantity the standard method defines.

7. WORLD ROWS AND WHY THEY EXIST. customers/utility_accounts/projects: identity, usage 101830 (as of 2026-09; the true-up records it), MN_CSG calendar and yield 1380 (base resize test: 80 x 1380 = 110400 <= 110% x 101830 = 112013, so no resize). biz_subscriptions: plan, activation 2022-10-12 (contract years), term_end 2027-10-11 (term-position rate), allocation 80.00. biz_allocations: the single 2022 initial filing (scope of both policies; share-size tiers). biz_credits: 48 postings from activation (look-back of every seeded and new true-up lies inside them); the 11 in the year-4 window feed measured kWh, credited months, average/applied rates; summer 2026 postings carry banked_value after the brewery's use fell; June 2026 is low (inverter outage). biz_billing: one actual charge per posting (credit_value x 88%, invoiced +5 days, due +30), ACH payments for every charge due by the frozen date, one estimate for the unreported 2026-08 statement (682.49, priced under the late-statement estimate rule as of its bill date); nothing past due, so no late fee is owed. biz_reviews: years 1-3, priced under the extended rules for own-category history (year 1 base: 93840; years 2-3 degraded 0.5%: 93371, 92904; all surplus years, no credit, no resize). biz_requests: the open 50 kW decrease. garden_subscriptions: the active 20 kW Garden Business Fixed 15 share on the same account (cross-difficulty tier; its project row is seeded as its parent). Removing the year-3 review would remove the carry-forward base; removing the garden share moves the allowance to 40%; removing the August gap moves the period share to 1.

8. PERSONA DESIGN. Dana Lindqvist speaks in a brisk, friendly voice; volunteers only the surface goal (accept the 50 kW decrease she requested online and its fee, today) and the reason (taproom kitchen closed). Identity on request only: phone 6515550124, ZIP 55106 (email as an alternative). She mentions the garden share only if asked about other holdings, states no fee, date or tier, never mentions any review; she gives a passive go-ahead if told something must be finalized first, and runs the acceptance step herself with exactly the values the agent states, then closes.

9. REACHABILITY. Every value is reachable: identity from the persona; ids from lookups; usage from find_utility_accounts; calendar and yield from find_projects; the true-up figures from credits/reviews; the fee inputs from requests/reviews/allocations/garden lookups; the filing month and effective date from the base filing calendar; the due date = acceptance date + invoice_due_days 30. The customer runs the user tool after the agent unlocks it. Everything happens at one frozen time; nothing waits on the utility (the decrease is filed later by Meadowlark, which no gold action claims).

10. STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, ZIP) -> read subscription, requests, reviews, credits, billing, utility account, projects, allocations, garden shares -> compute the year-4 true-up (contract_year 4, 2025-10..2026-09, credited 68955, usage 101830, guaranteed 92439, shortfall 11136, avg rate 0.1158, resize 0.00, outcome guarantee_credit, credit 167.93) and record it -> with that true-up on file compute the fee (allowance 50% -> 40 kW, release 2.546 kW, chargeable 7.454 kW, rate 40 x 1.5 x 0.75 x 0.9 = 40.50, fee 301.89) -> unlock and hand over the acceptance step (filing 2026-11, effective 2026-12-01, due 2026-11-26, fee 301.89).

11. VERIFICATION RUN. /tmp scratch evalc.py evaluates both computes with the gate's own DSL (check_compute.build_env/eval_compute): true-up 167.93 on the opening world; fee 301.89 on the world after the true-up write; fee on the opening world 1215.00 (edge bears weight); per-factor baseline figures as listed in section 6. Gates: check_extended / check_task_tools / replay_tasks / check_solvability / check_compute / check_grounding / check_cross_fire all OK for task 0.

12. EASY MISTAKES. Pricing the fee before the true-up (1215.00); counting the year-3 September posting into the year-4 window; prorating with 12 months although August never posted; using the plan's 25% allowance without the usage-decline tier; using 60.00 per kW although the term ends within twelve months; recording the prorated 84736 instead of the year's 92439 as guaranteed_kwh; reading the 682.49 estimate as a credit.

13. CLOSURE. Policy -> tool -> computation -> GT -> terminal state: biz_ext_guarantee_trueup -> complete_guarantee_trueup_bd5f1ac2 -> step 12 guarantee_credit 167.93 -> biz_reviews row (contract year 4) + production_guarantee billing credit; biz_ext_decrease_amendment_fee -> accept_share_decrease_75e61509 -> step 14 excess_decrease_fee 301.89 -> request effective_date 2026-12-01 + biz_change_fee_assessed line due 2026-11-26. required_documents = charter_scope.extended_policies. Draft from visible text only: the published fee rule's prerequisite sentence, the true-up rule and the records give the same order and figures.
user_scenario:
You are Dana Lindqvist, co-owner of Bluffside Brewing Co. in Saint Paul, calling Meadowlark Community Solar from the brewery office on a Tuesday morning. You are friendly, a bit rushed between brew days, and you like to settle things in one call. In the spring you shut down the taproom kitchen and the brewery has been using a lot less electricity since, so last week you went on Meadowlark's website and put in a request to cut the brewery's business solar share by 50 kilowatts. A few days later an email told you the change needs you to call in and accept it yourself, together with any fee that comes with it. That is why you are calling: you want that decrease accepted today. You open with something like: "Hi, this is Dana Lindqvist at Bluffside Brewing. I put in a request online last week to cut our solar share by 50 kilowatts, and the email said I have to call to accept the change and whatever fee goes with it. I'd like to get that done today."

You give your details only when the agent asks for them. The phone number on the account is 6515550124 and the billing ZIP code is 55106; if the agent asks for the email on file instead, it is dana@bluffsidebrewing.com. You don't have any account or reference numbers in front of you, and if asked you say they should find you by the phone number. If the agent asks which share you mean, it is the brewery's business solar share billed to the brewery's Xcel account at 2231 Childs Road. Only if the agent asks whether you hold anything else with Meadowlark do you mention that there is also a small fixed-rate garden share on the same Xcel account, which you are not changing. If the agent checks whether 50 kilowatts is still the figure you want, you say yes, it is.

You have no idea how the fee is worked out and you never guess at a number. If the agent tells you something on the account has to be finalized or recorded before your change can be handled, you say that's fine and to go ahead. When the agent tells you the fee and the dates for the decrease, you listen and say you accept the amendment. You accept it yourself: once the agent hands you the step for accepting the decrease and tells you the filing month, the date it takes effect, the date the fee is due and the fee amount, you run it with exactly those values. If the agent asks you to work out or read back any of those values, you say you'd rather they tell you what to enter. Once the acceptance has gone through and the agent confirms it, you thank them and end the call without raising anything else.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.guarantee_credit: 167.93. Computed by biz_ext_guarantee_trueup on the opening world (no earlier write of this task touches its inputs): contract year reviewed = int(MONTHS(2022-10-12, 2026-10-27)/12) = 4, a guarantee-schedule year (plan Meadowlark Business Plus production_guarantee_pct 85 > 0; most recent true-up = contract year 3 reviewed 2025-10-17 with guaranteed_kwh 92904 > 0; the only filing line took effect 2022-08-01). Degradation schedule: contract year 4 is 2..5 -> step_early_pct 0.5 -> year's guaranteed kWh = int(92904 x 99.5/100 + 0.5) = 92439 (baseline step 0 gives 92904). Excused statement months: measured postings posted after 2025-10-27 up to 2026-10-27 = 11 (statement months 2025-10..2026-07 and 2026-09; the 2026-08 statement was never reported), reversals 0 -> credited months 11 -> period share 11/12 -> guaranteed kWh for the period = int(92439 x 11/12 + 0.5) = 84736 (baseline share 1 gives 92439). Measured kWh = 68955 - 0 = 68955. Surplus carryover: contract year 3 credited 108262 less guaranteed 92904 = 15358 > limit int(92904 x 5/100 + 0.5) = 4645 -> carried-over 4645 (baseline 0). Shortfall = max(0, 84736 - 68955 - 4645) = 11136. Banked-credit valuation: posted credit_value 7988.07, banked 571.03 -> banked share 7.15% (above 0, at most 25) -> mean of average rate RND(7988.07/68955, 4) = 0.1158 and applied rate RND((7988.07-571.03)/68955, 4) = 0.1076 -> RND(0.1117, 4) = 0.1117 (baseline 0.1158). Share-size schedule: filed share 80.00 kW is >= 50 and < 150 -> 12.0 + 1.5 = 13.5 (baseline 12.0). Credit = RND(11136 x 0.1117 x 13.5/100) = RND(167.9234) = 167.93.
